Problem 2.  Given a positive integer n, Marie plays a game where she starts with the number 1
on a blackboard. As many times as she wants, she can choose an integer j such that 1        and                                                               V             ≤j ≤nreplace the number V on the blackboard with the number j R   j   . Here, R(x) denotes the nearest                                                                                               ·integer to x; if x is exactly halfway between two consecutive integers, it is rounded up. For example,
R(1.3) = 1 and R(1.5) = R(1.8) = 2.
  a) Prove that for each given n, there is a positive integer B such that Marie can never end up with
     a number larger than B on the blackboard.
  b) For any given n, let f(n) be the maximum number obtainable on the blackboard after finitely
    many replacements. Show that there exists a positive integer N such that for all n ≥N, we     have that 2026 divides f(n).
